sp.p: But he has already lived his life. Look, Clemenzia, I believe that it's clearly the will of God that she not be wasted like this, for He has taken pity on her virtue and on my poor soul. And so, lady Lelia, if you're willing, I don't want any other wife but you, and I swear to you as a knight that if you won't marry me, I'll never marry another.

sp.speaker: LELIA:
sp.p: Flamminio, you are my lord. You know exactly what I did and why, and so you know that I've never had any other desire but this.

sp.speaker: FLAMMINIO:
sp.p: You've proven it perfectly. Please forgive me if I've made you unhappy; not recognizing you. I'm very, very sorry, and I recognize my error.

sp.speaker: LELIA:
sp.p: You could never do anything, Signor Flamminio, that would make me unhappy.

sp.speaker: FLAMMINIO:
sp.p: Clemenzia, I don't want to wait any longer and take the chance that something unforeseen might ruin this good fortune. I want to marry her now if she's willing.

sp.speaker: LELIA:
sp.p: I'm most willing.

sp.speaker: CRIVELLO:
sp.p: Oh, thank God! And you, my master, Lord Flamminio, are you willing? By the way, you should know that I'm a notary. And if you don't believe me, here's my diploma.

sp.speaker: FLAMMINIO:
sp.p: I'm very willing and as happy as I've ever been in my life.

sp.speaker: CRIVELLO:
sp.p: Give each other your hands in marriage, and then you can go to bed. Oh! But I forgot to tell you that you should kiss her!

sp.speaker: CLEMENZIA:
sp.p: Here's what I think we should do now. You two stay here in my house while I go tell Virginio everything and break the bad news to Gherardo.

sp.speaker: FLAMMINIO:
sp.p: Fine, and you can tell Isabella as well.

p.seg: By the king's life, it's that old bag Pasquella who's trying to trick me out of my goods. How glad I am to have run into her.
Damn this pain in the ass! Just my luck to have him underfoot! He can break his neck along with all the others who have come from Spain, as far as I'm concerned! What excuse can I find now?

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Lady Pasquella!

p.seg: Things are going well, I've already become a lady.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: You've tricked me and taken my rosary, and you haven't done what you promised.

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Shush, shush, shush! Be quiet, be quiet!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Why? Is there someone around to hear us?

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Shush, shush, shush!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: I don't see anyone here. You're not going to deceive me again! What are you up to?

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: You're trying to ruin me.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: You're trying to tick me.

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Go away. Leave me alone now, and I'll talk with you later.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Give me back my rosary, and we can talk whenever you like. I don't want you to be able to say that you've deceived me.

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: I'll give it to you. But do you think I have it here? Do you think it's that important to me? Why, I can have all the rosaries I want!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Why did you lock me out and then start singing and say such strange things like "Ghost, ghost" and I don't know what prayers and other stuff?

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Be quiet. You're going to ruin me. I'll explain everything.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: What? Why don't you tell me?

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Move a little over this way, in this corner, so that my mistress won't see you.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Are you trying to trick me again?

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: You're so sure that I'm tricking you! Am I really the type of deceive someone? Is that what you think, eh?

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: All right, but tell me right now what's going on.

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Listen. When we were talking before, Isabella, my mistress, came down very quietly and was hidden near me and heard everything. When I was rounding up my chickens, she went into the room there and from a hole in the wall watched everything we did. I, realizing this, pretended that I hadn't seen her. And I pretended that I wanted to deceive you. In the end, when I showed her the rosary, she, believing that I had tricked you, took it away and, laughing, wrapped it around her arm. But I'll get it back tonight and give it to you if you don't want to me to have it.

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Is all this true? You'd better not be trying to deceive me!

sp.speaker: PASQUELLA:
sp.p: Dear Giglio, may I never see you again if it isn't true. Do you think I don't cherish your relationship? But you Spaniards don't believe in Christ or anything else!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Well, why don't we do now what we agreed to earlier?

p.seg: Oh, what a nuisance these Spaniards are!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: Tomorrow! Tomorrow morning, all right?

p.seg: Ugh, ugh, ugh! How disgusting!

sp.speaker: GIGLIO:
sp.p: I swear to God, I'll slash your face if you're deceiving me again!

sp.speaker: CITINA:
sp.p: I wonder what that strange noise is in the downstairs room. I hear the bed making a thumping, a drumming sound, as if it were possessed by some spirit. Oh my! I'm really scared. Oh! I hear someone, "My life, my happiness, my hope, my sweet dear wife!" Oh! I can't make out the rest. I tempted to knock. And oh! Now one of them says, "Wait for me." They must be getting ready to leave. And the other one is saying, "Come quickly too." It sounds like they're going to break that bed. Oh, oh, oh! That bed is bouncing so fast, so fast! By all that's ho ... hole ... holeym I'd better go tell Mama.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA:
sp.p: I was certain that you were the servant of a local knight. You look so much like him that you must be his brother.

sp.speaker: FABRIZIO:
sp.p: Others today have mistaken me for someone else. Even the innkeeper seemed confused.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA:
sp.p: Here comes Clemenzia, your balia. She'll want to speak with you.

p.seg: This must be him, for he looks exactly like Lelia.

sp.speaker: FABRIZIO:
sp.p: Excellent, my dear balia. How's Lelia?

sp.speaker: CLEMENZIA:
sp.p: Good, good. But let's go into the house, there's a lot I need to explain to you.

div2.head: SCENE VII

sp.speaker: VIRGINIO:
sp.p: I'm so happy to have found my son that I'm satisfied with everything.

sp.speaker: CLEMENZIA:
sp.p: It was all the will of God. It certainly has turned out better than if you had married your daughter off to that broken-down Gherardo. But let me go into the house to see how things are going. I left the newlyweds all alone and very, very close. [She goes in and after a moment calls] Come in, come in. Everything's fine.

div2.stage: [VIRGINIO follows her; STRAGUALCIA stops in the doorway]

sp.speaker: STRAGUALCIA:
sp.p: Spectators, don't wait for them to come back out of the house, because that will make a long story even longer. If you want to come to dinner with us, I'll be waiting for you at the Joker. And bring along some money, because no one's treating. But if you don't want to come – and it looks to me like that's the case - be happy and enjoy yourselves. And you members of the Intronati, how about some applause?
